# Lesson 6 Motherboards

## **Learning goals**

1. Understand the purpose motherboards serve  
2. Identify common components of a motherboard  
3. Explain the purpose of common motherboard components  
     
   

   

   Motherboards come in many shapes and sizes to fit the many devices they come in such as:

| ATX (standard), Micro-ATX (budget/small), Mini-ITX (ultra-compact), and specialized sizes like EATX (servers), Nano-ITX, and Pico-ITX for robots or IoT. |
| :---- |

   ![][image1]

   **Motherboard Scavenger Hunt\!**

   Use Google to look up the different pieces/ports of a Motherboard and fill in your copy of the chart.

|  | Function (What does it do/what connects to it) | Description (How do you recognize it) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **CPU Slot**  | Allows the CPU to connect to the motherboard. | Square/rectangular grid of golden dots. Slightly different shape depending on when it was made.  |
| **I/O Ports**  | Input/Output ports, allows for input/output devices to connect to the MoBo (external hard drives, mice, keyboards, monitors, etc) | Lots of ports of many shapes and sizes. Attached to the side of the motherboard.  |
| **PCI Slot**  | Allows for internal peripherals to attach to the motherboard (graphics cards, sound cards, more IO slots) | White or light blue rectangles with a split in the slot towards the right.  |
| **PCIe Slot** ![][image2] | Same as PCI, but with more bandwidth (faster). Is phasing out the PCI slot. | Dark blue or black (generally). Split is towards the left, or closer to the edge of the motherboard.  |
| **CMOS Battery** ![][image3] | Powers the BIOS (startup software).Also stores date and time information. | Silver disc battery |
| **ATX Power Connector** ![][image4] | Used to deliver power to the motherboard from the power supply. | White 2x12 grid plug  |
| **SATA Connectors** ![][image5] | Allows hard drives/SSDs/internal storage to connect to the motherboard. | L-shaped plug  |
| **RAM Slot** ![][image6] | Allows RAM to connect to the motherboard | Long rectangular slots, with clips on the ends. Usually groups of multiple next to each other.  |
